samples.xml_description:
<module id="pe">
    <description>Implement a Multiplying Accumulator for 32bit integer. In the MAC_PE, there is a register that stores the partial sum (the intermediate accumulation result), and in each cycle, the result of “a multiplied by b” will be accumulated in this register, and the “c” shows the value of the register.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst">Reset signal. Defined as 1 for reset and 0 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand A.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand B.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit output representing the accumulated result.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <enum id="PE_STATE_IDLE" value="2'b00">Idle state.</enum>
        <enum id="PE_STATE_MULT" value="2'b01">Multiplication state.</enum>
        <enum id="PE_STATE_ACC" value="2'b10">Accumulation state.</enum>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <enum_value id="state" value="PE_STATE_IDLE">State variable to track the current state of the PE.</enum_value>
        <enum_value id="next_state" value="PE_STATE_IDLE">Next state variable to determine the next state of the PE.</enum_value>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Implement a Multiplying Accumulator for 32bit integer. In the MAC_PE, there is a register that stores the partial sum (the intermediate accumulation result), and in each cycle, the result of “a multiplied by b” will be accumulated in this register, and the “c” shows the value of the register.</implementation>
</module>
